title: Deepen Townscaper technical research (confirmed via web search/fetch) and close the interior/room-generation gap the owner identified
objective: Owner-directed: having confirmed Townscaper as the chosen reference model for exterior procedural construction, the owner asked to capture everything Townscaper offers for VTT integration, and explicitly flagged noticing no coverage of interior generation. Researched via WebSearch/WebFetch (gamedeveloper.com's 'How Townscaper Works' technical article, BorisTheBrave's 'Wave Function Collapse tips and tricks', Steam community discussion, GDC Vault's Caves of Qud WFC talk, a Medium writeup on WFC+BSP dungeon generation) to (1) confirm and enrich the existing Townscaper technical description with previously-unrecorded details (real-time in-gameplay WFC resolution, two-pass structure-then-decoration generation, 'recipe' priority rules, silent-failure handling for unsatisfiable adjacency, performance-scaling caveat, >500 hand-authored tile modules), (2) explicitly confirm Townscaper has no interior/walkable-room generation at all -- verified absent from its own technical writeups and confirmed by its own community asking for the feature and not having it -- and (3) research the separate, complementary technique family (WFC applied to room/floorplan layout, the 'path constraint' global-connectivity enhancement, 'fixed tiles' pre-placement, BSP-partition-then-WFC-fill hybrid pipelines, Caves of Qud's professional multi-pass precedent) that closes the interior-generation gap, proposing how it integrates with the already-chosen ghx_proc_gen crate (same tool, different tileset/pass) rather than requiring a new dependency.
validations: Enriched the 'Reference model: Townscaper' section with newly web-confirmed technical details, each attributed to its source (gamedeveloper.com technical article; distinguished from the prior session's BorisTheBrave-sourced ~15-tile/256-configuration marching-cubes claim rather than silently merging the two different tile-count claims).

Added a new 'Interior generation (confirmed gap, and how to close it)' subsection: explicitly states Townscaper has no interior/room generation (confirmed via Steam community discussion and absence in its technical writeups), then documents the WFC-for-room-layout technique family (BorisTheBrave's room-tileset technique, the path-connectivity constraint, fixed-tile pre-placement mapping onto this document's existing four-tier model, BSP-partition-then-WFC-fill hybrid pipeline, Caves of Qud's professional multi-pass precedent) and proposes a concrete integration: reuse the already-chosen ghx_proc_gen crate with a second, interior-specific tileset/pass constrained by the building footprint the exterior generation already produces, rather than adopting a new dependency.

Recorded dominguerilla/wfc-dun-gen (GitHub) as a found-but-unverified reference (language, license, and API were not confirmed in this pass -- WebFetch on its README returned 404/no content) -- listed as a future thing to inspect, not cited as adopted or license-cleared.
Updated the open-items list to add: interior-specific WFC tileset/BSP design is undesigned (new item), and the wfc-dun-gen repo's license/language is unverified (new item).
No dependency installed, no code written, no ADR reopened -- documentation research/consolidation only, consistent with this document's stated non-normative research-catalog status.
artifacts: docs/research/vtt-map-and-terrain-construction-options.md (Townscaper section enriched; new interior-generation subsection added; open items updated)
risks: Web research reflects sources found today (2026-08-01) and may drift; the document's existing 'facts are dated and will drift' caveat applies unchanged.
